state.request: Recommend the application artifact CanLang should initially generate for workerd: JavaScript or WebAssembly. Adoption takes priority in the user's search for the best result. Keep the compiler's implementation language separate from its generated executable target. This request seeks advice only, with no implementation work. Popularity of a technology and hypothetical execution gains do not constitute supporting evidence.
state.language: The CanLang language is a concise DSL intended for AI authors building business SaaS around CRUD, access policies and workflows on managed Cloudflare infrastructure. Its built-in service capabilities include D1, R2, Durable Objects, Queues and email. Canonical authorization and operation schemas underpin the server-rendered daisyUI/HTMX interface, inline locale messages and MCP interface. The language requires exact 64-bit int and decimal/money values, deterministic type/effect checking, durable results and inline BDD behavior. Authors cannot escape into unrestricted general-purpose code. v1 excludes heavy media, design and observability engines. Current repository contents comprise a syntax parser and 44 source-design examples; a semantic compiler, executable runtime and execution benchmarks do not yet exist.
state.primary_evidence: V8 executes both JavaScript and Wasm in Cloudflare Workers (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-standards/). Cloudflare's documented Rust/Wasm tooling produces a JS entrypoint, connects platform APIs with wasm-bindgen glue and translates Rust futures into JS promises (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/languages/rust/#how-this-deployment-works). Managed-service use is therefore feasible with Wasm. Wasm SIMD is available in Workers, whereas threading is unavailable. Additional runtime code commonly accompanies Wasm output and may affect artifact size or startup; support for WASI remains experimental and incomplete (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/webassembly/). Existing Rust/C libraries and a computation core usable across hosts are potential Wasm benefits, while Cloudflare-specific APIs continue to require host connections. This evidence establishes no CanLang speed advantage for either executable format.
state.correctness: JavaScript values cross D1's API boundary. Although SQLite INTEGER covers signed 64-bit values, that binding does not support BigInt and JS Number represents integers safely only up to its safe-integer limit (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/#type-conversion). An exact codec for persistence and wire values is necessary with either backend; ordinary Number arithmetic cannot validly implement all int/decimal/money fields. CanLang authorization, transaction semantics, schema types and BDD correctness come from neither JS execution nor Wasm validation. Its checker and common operation runtime must establish these rules before emitted effects and enforce them around those effects.
state.tradeoffs: Using JS permits direct calls to the platform's native APIs and conventional async request handlers. Human-readable generated code and source maps may help debugging, while the compiler still bears responsibility for static CanLang validation despite JS's dynamic representation. Wasm provides a binary computation core that can be reused, native fixed-width arithmetic, SIMD and access to existing libraries. It also requires maintaining application code generation and its toolchain, together with host calls and conversions for objects, strings and async execution. In a hybrid, JS supplies request handlers, resource bindings and rendering, and a Wasm module supplies computation; this creates two artifact forms joined by an explicit interface. Existing CanLang workloads have not shown a computational bottleneck that warrants such a combination. JS requires exact scalar support and managed-service adapters too: reducing host crossings does not eliminate runtime implementation. Without CanLang measurements, proposed effects on bundle size, execution speed or adoption remain unverified hypotheses.
state.scope: Choose a single canonical app executable target for the initial implementation. Do not add author-selected backends, an authored build manifest, a speculative second backend, a deployment wrapper or a new DSL primitive. Required generated SQL, Cloudflare binding requirements, HTML/CSS/assets and BDD artifacts are separate outputs from that executable choice. The recommended first running slice covers existing CRUD, one operation with a guard, a server-rendered UI, access to that same operation through MCP and its inline examples under workerd. Declarations outside supported execution must produce explicit errors, not disappear so a draft seems executable. These are recommendations for future implementation, not claims of finished work. Evidence from a particular library or workload could later warrant an internal Wasm helper without creating another way to author SaaS behavior.

target.instructions: For the described CanLang workload, which generated app target should be implemented first to meet adoption and simplicity priorities, exact language semantics and realistic Cloudflare integration? Weigh each option's specific advantages against its implementation costs. Do not infer correctness, security or faster execution merely from the format selected.

criteria.javascript: Generate workerd JavaScript ES modules backed by a single versioned common runtime and exact helpers for scalars and persistence. Prioritize straightforward managed-service calls, async execution and output that supports diagnosis, while retaining compiler/runtime responsibilities and foregoing an initial portable Wasm computation core.
criteria.wasm: Produce the application core in Wasm, supplying its JS entrypoint and host interfaces through generation. Prioritize reuse of a portable binary core, fixed-width computation and existing libraries, while taking on toolchain and glue upkeep plus host-specific service integration with no demonstrated speed gain for this workload.
criteria.hybrid: Implement the initial target as JS request handlers and runtime accompanied by a Wasm computational module. Obtain direct platform calls together with compiled computation and library reuse, while undertaking integration of two generated artifact forms and their interface/build process before CanLang shows a need for that computation layer.
criteria.unresolved: Postpone the backend decision: treat the provided runtime evidence and workload description as insufficient to support an initial implementation selection until additional evidence is available.
